sequence.description: Bros notice a man at the tram stop with pigeons on his shoulders

sequence.speaker: lord_pilsner
sequence.dialogue: Hey, excuse me? Do you know how to get to the Velvet Curtain Club from here?

sequence.speaker: jiri
sequence.dialogue: The 17 should be here any moment. The schedule says... ah, the schedule is from 1994. But still.

sequence.speaker: jiri
sequence.dialogue: Yes. The 17. I have a good feeling about today. Today feels like a tram day.

sequence.speaker: bradley
sequence.dialogue: Sir, do you know how long you've been waiting?

sequence.speaker: jiri
sequence.dialogue: My wife asked me to pick up milk. That was in 2003. The milk will be VERY fresh when I return.

sequence.speaker: lord_pilsner
sequence.dialogue: ...So you don't know where the club is?

sequence.speaker: jiri
sequence.dialogue: I know where EVERYTHING is. I have had time to think about the layout of this city. The club is three blocks north. But you could also take the 17. When it arrives.

sequence.speaker: jiri
sequence.dialogue: *looks hopeful*

sequence.speaker: jiri
sequence.dialogue: *sighs, returns gaze to tracks*

variants.jiri_comment: The 22 mocks me with its regularity.

sequence.description: Player chooses to stay with Jiří through the night
sequence.speaker: jiri
sequence.dialogue: You are staying? No one stays. The pigeons stay, but pigeons do not understand conversation.

sequence.speaker: jiri
sequence.dialogue: Since you are staying... I will tell you why I wait.

sequence.speaker: jiri
sequence.dialogue: My wife asked me to get milk. Just milk. I said I would be back in twenty minutes.

sequence.speaker: jiri
sequence.dialogue: I had a ring in my pocket. I was going to propose when I returned. With the milk.

sequence.speaker: jiri
sequence.dialogue: The 17 never came. I waited. And waited. I thought, 'Just a few more minutes.'

sequence.speaker: jiri
sequence.dialogue: A few more minutes became... years. And now I cannot leave. If I leave, all the waiting was for nothing.

sequence.speaker: jiri
sequence.dialogue: She waited too. Then she stopped waiting. I do not blame her.

sequence.speaker: jiri
sequence.dialogue: The 17 is not about the tram anymore. It is about finishing something. Anything.

sequence.speaker: jiri
sequence.dialogue: You stayed. No one has ever stayed. The pigeons stay, but they do not understand. You understand.

sequence.speaker: jiri
sequence.dialogue: Heavy is the head that waits for the 17. But lighter now. Thank you.

sequence.speaker: lord_pilsner
sequence.dialogue: Bro... that was heavy.

sequence.speaker: jiri
sequence.dialogue: *stands slowly* That sound... I know that sound...

sequence.speaker: jiri
sequence.dialogue: *sits back down* False alarm. But for a moment... for a moment I believed.

sequence.speaker: jiri
sequence.dialogue: You are good people. Strange, but good. The locals will know you now. You sat with Jiří.

interactive_objects.description: A yellowed timetable behind cracked plastic. The date reads 1994. Someone has circled the #17 line obsessively in red pen. Handwritten notes fill every margin: 'Any day now.' 'The 17 WILL come.' 'I believe.'
interactive_objects.player_note: (This schedule is older than some of your party members.)

interactive_objects.description: Bread for the pigeons. Fruit that Jiří never eats. Handwritten notes from strangers. Photos of families he's never met. A small ecosystem of respect.

progressive_content.visit_5: Candles have been added. Someone is actively maintaining this.
progressive_content.visit_10: Children's drawings of Jiří and a tram labeled '17'. Fresh flowers, changed daily.
progressive_content.visit_13: A small bronze plaque: 'JIŘÍ'S BENCH - HE WAITED'

interactive_objects.description: A worn leather satchel bulging with papers. The visible pages show meticulous logs: tram numbers, times, dates. 47,000 entries. None of them say '17'.
interactive_objects.player_note: (This is either dedication or madness. Maybe both.)

interactive_objects.description: The seat next to Jiří. There's a pigeon on it, but it looks like it might move.

environmental_easter_eggs.description: An old newspaper clipping pinned to the shelter: 'LOCAL MAN VOWS TO WAIT FOR TRAM' - dated 2002
A faded missing person poster with Jiří's face. The word 'FOUND' is written across it in marker, along with 'He's at Stop 17.'
An old photo of Debaucheryville from the 1990s. In the background, at Tram Stop #17, the same man sits in the same position.

after_visit_3.speaker: lord_pilsner
after_visit_3.dialogue: That guy REALLY knows the transit system. We should ask him about the metro too.

after_visit_5.speaker: bradley
after_visit_5.dialogue: He's clearly a transportation expert. Did you see his documentation? 47,000 entries.

after_visit_7.speaker: chadwick
after_visit_7.dialogue: I respect his commitment to local transit. That's REAL European culture.

bros_misunderstanding.narrator_note: They never understand he's been trapped there by his own stubbornness.

narrator_commentary.on_first_visit: Tram Stop #17. Where patience becomes performance art and public transit becomes philosophy.
narrator_commentary.on_jiri_backstory: Jiří had waited so long that waiting had become his identity. The tram was almost beside the point now.
narrator_commentary.on_night_vigil_completion: The bros had done something unexpected. Something human. They stayed.
narrator_commentary.on_blessing: Locals would now nod at them with new respect. They were 'the Americans who sat with Jiří.' It meant something here.
